searchText: Looks like zkSync has a withdrawal queue that you can enter with a transaction on L1. If your tx is not processed within a week by the operator, the contract changes state and lets everyone withdraw with a single L1 transaction Hey. I’m a STEM teacher who has a love for Ethereum. I would love to help any way I can with the education side of things. Are there any problems (education) that need to be solved? So many. * Teaching people how to appropriately secure their assets. * Teaching people how gas works (though probably best to wait until EIP-1559 launches). * Teaching people how to secure recovery words. * Teaching people what it means to be ones own bank. Writing guides / videos? Or more hands on aka workshops? Guides/videos I think are valuable. There is a ton of stuff already out there, but it is difficult to find *quality* content in my experience. Agreed. Most of it is written for the wrong audience I would like to see more stuff targeting total newbies. That helps them get a grasp on the basics like what it means to "be your own bank" and when it is appropriate/reasonable to choose that over a custodial solution. Not everyone *should* be their own bank, but also not everyone should use a custodial solution. Now that is something I could work with. Teaching Elementary kid students how to use Python is my speciality. 🙂 if I can get kids to understand something I can try helping adults 😛 In my experience, children are *far* easier to teach than adults. 😛 Though, maybe we should just teach the kids, and then the kids will teach the adults. 😄 😛 sounds like bad experiences haha Perhaps some online educational content targeting 4-10 year olds on monetary policy? 😬 That’s what I usually do. Kids teaching the adults. Might be a good way to go about doing it actually Unfortunately, at the moment Ethereum is too expensive for "kids" to use. 😢 Testnet idea maybe? I think we would want to get some layer 2 solution out there specifically for that if we wanted to target that demographic. Or layer 2. I’ve been using loopring lately and it’s been super fun Yeah, testnet content could work. Or private network. Teaching kids how to code a smart contract could be fun By kids probably middle school/ high school for that I currently use Minecraft to teach kids Python Are you familiar with CrypotZombies? Of course I did the tutorials last year Really fun and interactive If you want to teach people to code (not just use Ethereum) then there is a lot of opportunity similar to CryptoZombies I think. But something where people with no coding knowledge can also participate. Artist can design the website. Etc I have had a number of people express interest to me in learning to write dapps, but they aren't starting with a programming background and they get a bit stuck on CryptoZombies. Exactly! Thanks for the ideas. I’ll let them stew for a bit and come back with some proposals. Mind if I dm them to you? You can, though I recommend proposing them here to get more eyes. 🤔 just realized this channel is in ETH2-RESEARCH category, I wonder why that is. Will do! If you want me to post somewhere else just let me know 🙂 Originally this whole discord server was focused on Eth2. The education channel just stuck in place. We could either move it to another category, or create an additional eth1 education channel. What do you think is better? I would prefer a general education channel I think. Based on history of this channel, I don't think we need to worry about too much content to overwhelm a single shared channel. 🙂

excerpts.content: Looks like zkSync has a withdrawal queue that you can enter with a transaction on L1. If your tx is not processed within a week by the operator, the contract changes state and lets everyone withdraw with a single L1 transaction
